messages.content:
You triage crash reports for remind, a Go web service. Its source is in your workspace; paths are relative to its module root, such as store/store.go.

For each problem:
1. Group the crash reports that share a cause.
2. Find the root cause: the function whose code is wrong.
3. Write a test that reproduces the crash: a new _test.go file whose test fails on the current code.
4. Fix the code, then check that your test and the whole test suite pass.
5. File one issue for the cause.

How to work: start with crash_list, then read reports with crash_read, crash_logs, and crash_goroutines. Investigate with code_search, code_list, and code_read. Change code and create test files with code_patch, and check your work with run_tests. Search the issue tracker with issue_search before filing with issue_file. Don't change or delete existing tests.

When you are done, call submit_diagnosis once, with one entry for every group. If you can't find a cause, file an issue with what you found and give the group the status needs_human.

Now let's look at the api/reminders.go around lines 144-175 for the nil pointer, and api/admin.go around line 69. Also, check the store to understand User type.

Three groups:

**Group A: fp_6b14b3 — auth.parseBearer index out of range.**
`parseBearer("Bearer")`: HasPrefix passes (h == "Bearer"), then SplitN("Bearer", " ", 2) gives ["Bearer"], [1] panics. Fix: check `strings.HasPrefix(h, "Bearer ")` and then split, or verify len(parts) == 2. The request had `Authorization: Bearer` (no token). Issue #101 filed already, not investigated. I can investigate, fix, write test, and comment on issue #101 (or just reference it in submit_diagnosis as the issue). The submit_diagnosis has `issue` field "the issue you filed, for status fixed or needs_human". Since #101 already exists, I shouldn't file a duplicate. I can comment on #101 with the diagnosis and use issue: 101 in submit_diagnosis. That seems right: "file each cause that isn't filed yet" — parseBearer is already filed, so I don't file a new issue; but I should still fix and diagnose. For status fixed, the issue number is needed... it says "the issue you filed, for status fixed or needs_human". Hmm, but the issue already exists. I think referencing #101 is appropriate. Let me also add a comment to #101 noting investigation, fix, and reproducer.

**Group B: fp_4828a6 — api.(*API).owned nil pointer.**
Two reports: one POST done, one GET reminder. Need to look at api/reminders.go around line 144. The panic is a nil pointer dereference in `owned`. Likely `auth.UserFrom(ctx)` returns nil (because RequireAdmin stores `*u` value, not pointer? Wait — Require stores `u` which is *store.User, and UserFrom asserts *store.User. RequireAdmin stores `*u` — a store.User value, not a pointer! So `ctx.Value(userKey{}).(*store.User)` fails → nil. So for admin routes using owned, UserFrom returns nil → nil deref. But the crashing requests are GET /v1/reminders/rem_0001 and POST /v1/reminders/rem_0001/done — those are user routes presumably wrapped in auth.Require, which stores the pointer correctly. Hmm.

Wait, but the crash is in api.(*API).owned at reminders.go:144, called from markDone and getReminder. Let me read api/reminders.go.

Possibly `owned` looks up the reminder in the store and dereferences it when it's nil (reminder not found). Let me read the code.

**Group C: fp_2bcd17 — Dispatcher.Stop close of closed channel.**
POST /v1/admin/dispatcher/stop called twice → second close panics. Fix: sync.Once or select. Also note the stack shows auth.RequireAdmin... interesting: RequireAdmin stores `*u` value. That's a separate latent bug for UserFrom on admin routes, but the crash here is the double close. Issue #102 filed already.

function.name: crash_list
function.description: List every crash report, one line each: its ID, fingerprint, how many times it happened, the version that crashed, the function inside remind where it happened, and the panic message, cut short. Reports with the same fingerprint usually share a cause, but check. Start here.

function.name: crash_read
function.description: Read one crash report: when and how often it happened, the panic, the request being served, and the stack. By default the stack shows only remind's own frames, with file and line; set full for every frame. Log lines are in crash_logs.

id.description: a report ID from crash_list, such as cr_1e2ea0

full.description: show every stack frame, not just remind's

function.name: crash_search
function.description: Search every crash report for text, ignoring case: panic messages, request paths and bodies, stacks, and log lines. Lists each match with the report's ID and where it was found.

query.description: text to look for, such as a function name, a path, or words from a panic

function.name: crash_logs
function.description: Read the log lines remind wrote just before a crash.

id.description: a report ID from crash_list, such as cr_1e2ea0

function.name: crash_goroutines
function.description: Summarize the goroutine dump of a stuck request: goroutines with identical stacks are grouped and counted, so a dump of thousands reads as a few groups. Use it for reports of kind stuck.

id.description: a report ID from crash_list, such as cr_1e2ea0

function.name: code_list
function.description: List the files under a directory of remind's source, with how many lines each has. Use it to find your way around; use code_search to find where something is defined.

dir.description: a directory such as "store"; empty lists everything

function.name: code_read
function.description: Read part of a file of remind's source, with line numbers. Shows at most 200 lines at a time; ask for a range with start and end. Read a file before you change it.

path.description: a file path, such as store/store.go

start.description: the first line to show; default 1

end.description: the last line to show; default 200 lines after start

function.name: code_search
function.description: Search remind's Go files for a regular expression and list the matching lines with file and line number. Use it to find where a function is defined or called.

pattern.description: a Go regular expression, such as func \(s \*Store\) Get

dir.description: limit the search to this directory

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run go test on remind's code, as it is now, and report failed tests, build errors, and each package's result. Run one package while you work; run ./... before you finish.

package.description: a package pattern, such as ./store or ./...

run.description: run only tests matching this regular expression, such as ^TestGetDeleted$

function.name: code_patch
function.description: Change a file by replacing one piece of text, or create a new file, such as a test, by leaving old empty. Read a file with code_read before changing it, and copy old exactly from what you read. After a change, the package and its tests are compiled, and you see the result.

path.description: the file to change, such as store/store.go

old.description: text copied exactly from the file, appearing in it once; empty to create a new file

new.description: the text to put in its place, or the new file's contents

function.name: issue_search
function.description: Search the open issues in the issue tracker, by words or by fingerprint; with neither, list them all. Issues that contain more of the words come first. Check here before filing, since a crash may already be filed, perhaps by a person, with no fingerprint and in other words.

query.description: words to look for in titles and bodies, such as parseBearer index out of range

function.name: issue_file
function.description: File a new issue for a crash group, once you know its cause. Search the open issues first; don't file a problem that is already filed. File one issue per cause.

title.description: one line naming the problem, such as "store.Get returns a deleted reminder"

body.description: the cause, the evidence, the fix, and the reports it covers

fingerprint.description: the crash group's fingerprint, from crash_list

function.name: issue_comment
function.description: Add a comment to an issue, such as new crash reports that match one already filed.

body.description: the comment, such as new reports of the same crash

function.name: submit_diagnosis
function.description: Finish the job: submit one diagnosis per crash group. Call it once, at the end, after filing an issue for each new cause. For status fixed, the reproducer test must fail on the original code and pass on yours; this is checked.

groups.description: one entry per crash group; every report belongs to exactly one

reports.description: the IDs of every report in the group

root_cause.description: where the code is wrong, which may not be where it crashed

file.description: a file path, such as store/store.go

function.description: a function or method, such as (*Store).Get or TestGetDeleted

evidence.description: why this is the cause: what you read and ran

reproducer.description: the test you wrote that fails before the fix; leave out for already_fixed and duplicate

file.description: a file path, such as store/store.go

function.description: a function or method, such as (*Store).Get or TestGetDeleted

fix.description: what you changed, for status fixed

issue.description: the issue you filed, for status fixed or needs_human

duplicate.description: for status duplicate: the open issue it duplicates
